definition: Mean shift is a non-parametric feature-space mathematical analysis technique for locating the maxima of a density function, a so-called mode-seeking algorithm.
details: Application domains include cluster analysis in computer vision and image processing.

explainer.lead: Mean shift finds the peaks of a data density by sliding each point toward where its neighbours are densest. It matters because it clusters data without being told the number of clusters in advance.

tiers.eli5: Imagine dropping marbles on a hilly surface: each one rolls uphill until it settles at the top of a hill, and marbles on the same hill belong together.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it for clustering and for tracking objects in video, since it needs no fixed cluster count. A pitfall is choosing the window size: too small fragments clusters, too large merges them, and cost grows with the data.
tiers.paperLevel: For each point x, repeatedly set x = sum of K(x_i - x) * x_i divided by sum of K(x_i - x) over nearby points, until the shift is below a tolerance. Convergence depends on the kernel bandwidth, which is a user-set parameter.

explainer.example: Points scattered around two centres, at 0 and at 10, each drift to their nearest dense centre, producing two clusters without specifying two beforehand.
